title: UVs and materials
sub: How a picture gets onto a model, and why metal shines
cards/0/title: How to stick a picture on 3D
cards/0/body:
To paint a model with a picture (a texture), each vertex gets a second set of coordinates, UV: where on the picture this point sits. U is horizontal, V is vertical, both from 0 to 1.

This is an unwrap: like cutting open a cardboard box and laying it flat on a table.
cards/1/title: A material is what an object is made of
cards/1/body:
A material says how a surface reflects light. The modern approach is PBR (physically based rendering): base color, metallic and roughness.

The same numbers look almost the same in different programs, which is why PBR became the standard.
cards/1/deep: glTF uses the metallic-roughness model: baseColor, metallic, roughness, normal, occlusion, emissive, plus extensions (transmission, clearcoat, sheen). Older formats such as OBJ with .mtl and Collada describe materials with Phong: diffuse, specular, shininess. Those materials transfer poorly between programs.
cards/2/q: Which glTF line says the material is metal?
cards/2/explain: metallicFactor = 1 means metal. 0 means a dielectric: plastic, wood, stone.
cards/3/q: A vertex has UV = (0.5, 0.5). Where is it on the texture?
cards/3/options/0: In the center of the picture
cards/3/explain: Both coordinates are halfway through the 0 to 1 range.
cards/4/q: metallic = 1, roughness = 0. What does it look like?
cards/4/explain: Metal with zero roughness reflects like a mirror. The higher the roughness, the blurrier the highlight.
cards/5/body:
Pictures either sit as separate files next to the model (OBJ + .mtl + .png, glTF + .bin + .png) or live inside a single file (GLB, USDZ, FBX with embedded textures).

Separate files are easy to lose when you send them, hence the eternal “the model arrived gray”.
cards/6/q: Someone sent you model.obj, and in the viewer it is gray. Why?
cards/6/options/0: They did not include the .mtl and textures: OBJ keeps materials separately
cards/6/explain: OBJ points to material.mtl with an mtllib line, and that file points to the pictures. No files, no color.
cards/7/pairs/0/1: Where a point lies on the picture
cards/8/q: What does a glTF PBR material describe? Select all.
cards/8/explain: A material is about the surface. Geometry and files are not its concern.
